questions.q: What does a Fabric tenant map to, per this lesson?
options: A single Fabric workspace
The organization's Microsoft Entra ID — the same tenant Power BI already uses
One lakehouse item
A single capacity's region
questions.explain: A Fabric tenant is the top-level governance boundary and maps one-to-one with the organization's Microsoft Entra ID, the same identity tenant Power BI already uses.

questions.q: What is a capacity, as defined in this lesson?
options: A synonym for the tenant itself
The compute and governance unit that workspaces are assigned to, with its own region and its own admins
A single Power BI report
A backup copy of the tenant's data
questions.explain: A capacity — an F-SKU or trial capacity — is what every workspace runs on. It has its own region and its own capacity admins, distinct from tenant admins.

questions.q: Why might an organization run multiple capacities under one tenant?
options: It's required by Fabric and cannot be avoided
To split compute and governance by region or business unit while staying under one tenant
Because each Power BI report needs its own capacity
Multiple capacities are not actually possible in Fabric
questions.explain: One tenant can hold many capacities, commonly split by region (US, UK, Germany in the lesson's diagram) or by business unit, while remaining under a single organizational tenant.

questions.q: What does 'delegating' a tenant setting to capacity admins actually change?
options: It deletes the setting from the tenant entirely
It lets capacity admins control that specific setting themselves for their own capacity's workspaces, without a tenant admin acting each time
It gives capacity admins full tenant-admin rights over every setting
It has no effect — only tenant admins can ever change settings
questions.explain: Delegation is the structural reason tenant admins don't have to manage every governance decision centrally forever — a delegated setting can be controlled by capacity (or workspace) admins themselves.

questions.q: What does the diagram in this lesson show?
options: Two retail companies, both following the same tenant-to-capacity-to-workspace shape (one of them, company B, even runs two separate tenants)
A single company with no capacities at all
A comparison between Fabric and a competing product
A step-by-step wizard for creating a new workspace
questions.explain: Microsoft's own diagram shows Retail company A as one tenant with three regional capacities, and Retail company B as two separate tenants, each independently following the same tenant/capacity/workspace structure underneath.
